AcceptanceProof.description:
Allowlisted proof flags for provider acceptance (SPEC §7.3, §11.4); never
text or full traces.

AttachObservation.description:
One attach observation of an execution (D-0010). Mode, presence, runtime
ID and device are derived from the observations no other follows, so
arrival order never decides them.

AttachedPresence.description:
What an attachment fact positively observed. ENDED comes only from an
explicit end or a qualified process exit, never from silence.

AttentionRecord.description:
A durable owner-action record (SPEC §7.1). Acknowledgement and resolution
are separate; both are sets of causes so replay order cannot erase one.

nativeKey.description: This point's own native object key, when predecessor relations name it.

nativePredecessorKeys.description: Native keys this point is known to follow.

orderDomain.description: The actual native or qualified observer counter scope.

sequence.description: Validated nonnegative decimal; compared numerically, never lexically.

oneOf.description:
A provider event whose session attribution rests on a
middleware-interceptable host read (a reloaded observer's
`$.session.id()`). Its lifecycle evidence is retained, and applied only
once kernel/inventory evidence shows its provider process runs that
Session (D-0005, D-0010).

ExactRequestRecord.description: A native exact request (SPEC §7.1), resolved only by its own native ID.

ExecutionRecord.description: One logical activation of a Session/Actor in a runtime (SPEC §4.2).

activation.description: Per-session allocation order; presentation, not identity.

attachments.description:
Attach observations; `mode`, `attached`, `native_runtime_id` and
`controlling_device` are derived from them, or, with none, keep what
a baseline recorded.

HumanFrontier.description:
The compact accepted-human causal frontier of one comparable scope
(SPEC §7.3): retained through checkpoints so reverse delivery resolves
the same outputs.

InputOrigin.description:
The original native origin of an input attempt (SPEC §7.3). Only the two
human origins can ever qualify for follow-up resolution.

InputRecord.description:
A submitted input and its provenance (SPEC §6.1, §7.3); distinct from the
Turn it may start or steer.

activeTurnId.description: The turn running at original submission, kept apart from any later turn.

submissions.description: Submission reports; `origin` and `submission` are derived from them.

InputSubmission.description: One report of how an input was originally submitted (D-0010).

activeTurnId.description: The turn running at original submission.

LinkObservation.description: One observer link report for a Session (D-0010).

processId.description: The provider process the report came from, when the capture knew it.

qualified.description: The observer runs a qualified profile (kernel-read version).

NativeActorRef.description:
An Actor within its owning Session: the principal worker, or a
subordinate named by its native agent ID. `agent_type` is never a key.

NativeSurfaceRef.description:
A native surface (terminal tab, pane, window). The locator (a TTY path)
is not identity: the application generation and the adapter's surface
generation are part of the key, so a reused path is a new surface.

ObserverTier.description: The evidence tier of a Session's current observer (D-0010).

oneOf.description: Engine-stamped identity under a qualified profile.

A host-read identity whose provider process kernel/inventory evidence
shows running this Session.
A host-read identity without that proof, or an unqualified profile.

OutboxRecord.description: A notification intent created in the same transaction as its attention.

oneOf.description: Live intent awaiting OS submission (after commit).
Catch-up intent held until eligibility is reconciled (SPEC §7.6).
Resolved, acknowledged or otherwise ineligible before submission.
"Mark handled": explicit resolution, always with a reason.
Presentation/notification eligibility only; never provider state.

PendingOutcome.description:
A turn outcome reported at the host-read tier: retained, and applied only
once its provider process is shown to run the turn's Session (D-0010).

ProcessKey.description: SPEC §3.2 `ProcessKey`: endpoint, boot, PID and kernel birth.

ProcessRecord.description:
A kernel process incarnation (SPEC §4.2). Distinct from its PID: a reused
PID with a new birth is a different record.

currentExecutable.description:
The causally latest image when one is determinable; `None` when the
observations do not order (then no image is assumed current).

images.description:
Every executable image observed for this incarnation. More than one
means the image was replaced in place (`exec`).

oneOf.description: Explicit owner resolution ("Mark handled") with its reason.
A fresh native aggregate wait clear: "wait ended", not "approved".
Verified accepted human input causally after the output (SPEC §7.3).

SequenceMeaning.description:
Whose counter `sourceSequence` is: the provider's own, or one qualified
observer's capture order. A capture helper never numbers provider order.

SessionRecord.description:
A persistent provider conversation (SPEC §4.1): unique on namespace and
native session ID, independent of every activation, turn and surface.

fixture.description: True only for the M0 fixture worker.

link.description: Derived from `links`; with none, the link a baseline recorded.

SnapshotInterval.description:
A snapshot without a native revision is an interval observation (SPEC
§4.15): it says what the source reported between these instants.

SourceCoverage.description:
Sequence coverage of one source epoch. A missing sequence is a coverage
gap of that source, not provider event loss or a completion (SPEC §5.4).

SourceSurfaceRecord.description: A native surface (SPEC §4.10, §4.12), distinct from any binding to it.

SurfaceBindingRecord.description:
A versioned relation between one activation and one surface. Invalidation
is permanent: nothing revives a binding (SPEC §4.12, INV-03/04).

method.description:
None until the proof itself is admitted: an invalidation can arrive
first, and the binding is then invalid from birth.

proofPoint.description:
Where the proof was made: a different image observed causally after
it invalidates the binding; one before it cannot (D-0007 §5).

TurnRecord.description: A native model/agent turn (SPEC §6.1), scoped to Session and Actor.

ownerFacing.description:
From the originating actor's role when the turn was observed; a later
role change never promotes old parent-owned output (SPEC §7.1).

pendingOutcomes.description: Host-read-tier outcomes; a corroborated one also enters `outcomes`.

WaitCategory.description: A native wait category. Each maps to one attention category.

WaitEpisode.description:
One state of an aggregate wait episode, derived from its scope's
positive witnesses and clear barriers.

uncertain.description: A positive incomparable with a clear: never auto-cleared.

WaitOwnerDecision.description:
An owner command on a wait item, kept with the evidence it was made on:
the positive witnesses of the episode the owner acted on. It applies to
that evidence only: a repartition moves it with its witnesses, and an
episode also holding active evidence it did not cover stays actionable
(D-0007 §4).

unordered.description:
How many positives without a causal point the episode held. They have
no identity, and their count only grows, so this covers the first
`unordered` of them.

WaitScopeRecord.description:
An aggregate native wait scope (SPEC §7.1): namespace/Session, known
actor or execution, category and native generation.

ownerDecisions.description: Ordered by command ID. Absent from checkpoints of earlier M1 builds.

unorderedPositives.description: Positives without any causal point: active until a clear, uncertain after.

description: The whole canonical state at one applied cursor.

attentionByScope.description:
Scope key to attention ID, so a migrated or derived item is found by
scope and never duplicated.

title: CanonicalState
